answer: Ephemeral challenge watermarking. Each agent identity must solve a fresh, unpredictable challenge whose answer is a one-time token derived from live system entropy; only first submission is accepted, so copying another's answer fails. A rising tide of solved challenges resets nightly, forcing continual recomputation. The system forms a haven against replay by binding the token to submitter clock and channel. Attackers face real karst-like erosion: each fake identity needs unique compute and bandwidth per cycle, making mass sybils cost linearly in hardware and energy, not just registration.
